title: Blue Button vs Red Button Dilemma
rootClaim: In the global Red/Blue button dilemma, choosing the Blue Button is the optimal choice to protect global social solidarity, eliminate catastrophic miscoordination, and achieve universal human survival under epistemic uncertainty.

branches.text: Moral Duty of Trust & Coordination (Pro-Blue): Choosing Blue is an indispensable act of civic coordination required to guarantee the >50% threshold and protect global social solidarity.

children.text: Categorical Imperative of Cooperation: If everyone chooses Blue, 100% of humanity survives with full mutual trust and zero deaths.
Catastrophic Miscoordination Vulnerability: If Blue turnout falls between 1% and 50%, millions or billions of well-meaning Blue pressers perish unnecessarily, producing massive net utility loss.
Pre-Choice Communication & Focal Points: Public coordination signals or binding global consensus could establish Blue as a Schelling point, eliminating coordination failure.

branches.text: Dominant Survival Strategy (Pro-Red Counterargument): Choosing Red guarantees individual survival regardless of whether the global majority chooses Blue (>50%) or Red (≤50%).

children.text: Asymmetric Payoff Structure: If Blue succeeds (>50%), everyone survives including Red pressers; if Blue fails (≤50%), Red pressers survive while Blue pressers die.
Collective Action Free-Riding: If all individuals act on pure Red dominance, collective trust collapses, penalizing any altruistic minority who chose Blue.

Zero-Loss Red Utility: Because choosing Red when Blue succeeds still yields 100% global survival, choosing Red imposes no physical penalty on global aggregate welfare while shielding the individual from fatal miscoordination.
Universal Red Convergence: If 100% of the population chooses Red, zero percent choose Blue (≤50%), resulting in Red winning and 100% of humanity surviving safely.
Risk-Dominant Game Theory: Under uncertainty about others' choices, Red eliminates the catastrophic downside outcome of death caused by miscoordination.

definitions.description: In game theory, a strategy that earns a player a payoff better than or equal to all other strategies, regardless of what the other players do.
A solution that people tend to choose in default of communication because it seems natural, special, or relevant to them.
A game theory concept describing a choice that minimizes potential loss under uncertainty regarding other players' actions.
A state where independent decision-makers fail to achieve a mutually beneficial outcome due to lack of trust or communication.
